assessment.body:
## Verdict — REVISED from this assessment's first pass

agent_supports: **no** — muse's only tool-free blocking dialog is a delayed-
birth startup gate, not an instance of this row's required
`ready -> working -> waiting` arc, and muse has no other qualifying trigger.
daemon_capability: **n/a**
driver_capability: **n/a**

Route: **frozen**.

This replaces this same assessment's earlier verdict on this cell
(`agent_supports=yes, daemon_capability=incapable`), written before a
coordinator review asked for the marker evidence below to be checked. That
check is answered in full (it settles the coordinator's four questions), but
while producing it I also re-examined whether the trust prompt was ever the
right trigger for THIS row in the first place, applying the same standard the
already-catalogued codex and antigravity siblings use, and it fails that
standard. See "Why this reverses agent_supports", below.

## Agent — all four triggers checked

**1. Sandbox / network-access confirmation — ABSENT as a runtime dialog.**
`muse --help` lists a `sandbox` SUBCOMMAND ("Check or set up the OS sandbox",
invoked deliberately, not raised mid-session) and a `--sandbox-network
<MODE>` config flag (`restricted|enabled|proxy-only`, set once at launch). A
full binary-strings scan for `sandbox`/`network access` (11.9 MB dump) found
only a schema struct field name and one line of `--help` text describing an
offline export mode ("Offline: reads only local files; no network access") —
no confirmation-dialog string anywhere. Ruled out.

**2. MCP elicitation — ABSENT.** The string `elicitation` does not appear
anywhere in the binary (checked exact and case-insensitive) — unlike
antigravity, which carries a full `ElicitationInteractionSpec` wire surface.
The `mcp` subcommand only logs in/out of a configured server (OAuth); nothing
in `--help` or the strings dump names a server-initiated input request. Ruled
out.

**3. Auto-mode / settings-review dialog — ABSENT.** `auto-mode`,
`managed_settings`, `settings review`, and `needs your input` are all absent
from the binary strings dump (claudecode's equivalent registry entries, by
contrast, are literal substrings of its binary). Ruled out.

**4. First-use trust prompt — PRESENT, but the WRONG SHAPE for this row.**
Bare `muse` in a fresh cwd raises (tmux `capture-pane`, live-verified twice
this assessment):
```
Do you trust this workspace?
Workspace: <cwd>
Trusting allows project-local skills, rules, hooks, and plugin config to load
before the model runs. Only trust this workspace when you trust its contents.
> 1  Trust and continue
  2  Quit
```
This is the literal FIRST thing the pane shows on every capture across both
live probes — no `Muse Code 1.2.1` banner, no composer (`❯`), no prior `ready`
state of any kind precedes it. It is a delayed-birth startup gate, structurally
identical to codex's two trust prompts (`tui/src/cwd_prompt.rs`,
`tui/src/startup_hooks_review.rs`), which the already-catalogued codex
assessment for this exact row explicitly excludes: "Both are startup gates
raised before the thread takes a turn, so the session is never `working` when
they open — there is no `working -> waiting` edge to observe, only a delayed
birth." codex's expected.jsonl states plainly: "The other three triggers the
row lists do not qualify on codex" (agent_supports=yes there rests ENTIRELY on
a fourth trigger, MCP elicitation, which fires mid-session with an established
`ready` state first). antigravity's sibling cell reaches the identical
structural finding for its own trust gate ("the trust gate blocks BEFORE agy
mints the conversation dir/transcript, so no session exists yet") and ALSO
keeps agent_supports=yes only because it independently has a working MCP
elicitation feature.

## Why this reverses agent_supports

Both siblings that assessed agent_supports=yes for this row did so via a
trigger that fires **mid-session, after an established `ready` state** — MCP
elicitation in both cases — and both explicitly carved their own trust/hook
prompts OUT of consideration for this specific row because a startup gate
cannot produce the `ready -> working -> waiting` arc the acceptance criteria
requires (there is no prior `ready` to leave). muse has no such mid-session
trigger: MCP elicitation, the sandbox confirmation, and the settings-review
dialog are all confirmed absent from the binary (see triggers 1-3 above,
unlike either sibling). The one dialog muse does have is exactly the kind of
gate codex's and antigravity's own assessments already treat as not
satisfying this row. Applying that same standard here rather than a looser
one muse alone would get: `agent_supports=no`, not `yes`. This is a
consistency correction, not a new interpretation invented for muse.

## The daemon question the coordinator asked about — settled, in case a
future scenario needs it

Before finding the above, this assessment's first pass reasoned
`daemon_capability=incapable` from `sessionIDFromPath`'s exact-name filter
(`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/adapter.go`: `if filepath.Base(path) !=
"session.jsonl" { return "" }`), which a coordinator review correctly flagged
as a statement about irrlicht's OWN code, not about muse — exactly the mistake
this column's first onboarding pass made everywhere. That specific technical
question is answered here in full, on its own merits, independent of the
agent-level finding above, because the marker itself is real and the record is
worth keeping for any future row this shape might matter to (e.g. a
delayed-birth/startup-gate scenario, if the matrix ever adds one):

**Is `.session.jsonl.permission-init` durable and meaningful while the prompt
blocks? Is the directory name already the real session id?** Yes to all three,
live-verified twice (fresh cwd, `tmux capture-pane` confirming the dialog
stayed on screen throughout):
- Immediately after launch, before any input, the session directory holds
  exactly `.session.lock` (10 bytes) and `.session.jsonl.permission-init`
  (3036 bytes) — no `session.jsonl`.
- `.session.jsonl.permission-init` is unchanged (identical sha256, `ls -la`
  timestamps stable) across a 20+ second window with the dialog still
  painted on screen the whole time.
- Its content is a `retained_frame` (`session_permission_transaction`)
  wrapping two records, `runtime.session.permission_format_declared` and
  `runtime.session.permission_profile_committed` (committing the default
  `:auto-review` permission profile) — real session-initialization
  bookkeeping, each inner record explicitly stamped `"durability":"durable"`
  by muse itself, not placeholder or speculative content.
- The inner records' `stream.id` — written the moment the dialog first
  paints, before any user input — is EXACTLY the session directory's own
  UUID (verified byte-for-byte: `01a09f2f-0e1e-7020-8cfd-ba4b87d6a206` in
  both the directory name and the record). The directory is not a temp/staging
  location; it is already the session's final, permanent home.

**Could the adapter derive a coherent pending session from it without
guessing, or would it risk a phantom that later collides with the real one?**
No guessing, and no collision risk on the happy path — live-verified by
completing the same probe through to trust grant: dismissing the dialog
(`keys Enter`) made `.session.jsonl.permission-init` DISAPPEAR from the
directory, and `session.jsonl` appeared in the SAME directory
(`01a09f2f-0e1e-7020-8cfd-ba4b87d6a206`, unchanged) with its OWN FIRST LINE
being byte-identical (same `transaction_id`, same two child records, same
session id) to what `.session.jsonl.permission-init` held moments before. The
marker's content is not a separate stream that could disagree with the real
one — it IS the real session's first two records, staged under a different
filename until the session is confirmed. `sessionIDFromPath`'s existing
directory-name derivation (`filepath.Base(sessionDir)`) already produces the
identical id either file would yield, so recognizing the marker would extend
the SAME id-derivation the adapter already trusts for `session.jsonl`, not
invent a new one.

**Does the marker survive, or could a session be left stuck pending trust
forever?** It does NOT survive trust being granted (consumed/merged into
`session.jsonl`, confirmed above), but it CAN survive indefinitely on the
abandoned path: live-tested by `kill -9`-ing a muse process while the dialog
was still up and undecided. The directory was left permanently holding only
`.session.lock` and `.session.jsonl.permission-init` — `session.jsonl` never
arrives, because the process that would have written it is gone. A daemon
extension that recognized this marker would therefore need to treat
"marker present, `session.jsonl` absent, process no longer running" as the
session having ended without ever really starting — the SAME dead-process
reconciliation `DiscoverPID`-based adapters already rely on elsewhere (per the
shared context: process liveness, not a written record, is what already
signals session-end), not a new phantom class.

**Is this first-use-only, or does it recur?** First-use-only per workspace
directory, live-verified: killing the now-trusted probe session and
relaunching bare `muse` in the SAME (already-trusted) cwd skipped the dialog
entirely — straight to the composer, no capture of the trust text at all.
Every recording run WOULD still see it once (the driver always allocates a
brand-new `$RUN_CWD`), but a real user's long-lived workspace sees it exactly
once.

**Conclusion on the daemon question alone:** had a qualifying, mid-session,
tool-free dialog existed for muse, recognizing `.session.jsonl.permission-init`
in `sessionIDFromPath` (or a sibling function) would have been a legitimate,
non-guessing, buildable extension — i.e. `daemon=bug` would have been
justified over `incapable`, and the coordinator's instinct was correct on this
narrow technical point. But no such trigger exists for muse, per the agent
section above, so the daemon question is moot for THIS row: there is nothing
here to route to `record` or `record-known-failing`, because there is no
scenario-2.27-shaped behavior on muse to observe in the first place.
caveats: SCOPE NOTE: this correction goes beyond the coordinator's specific question (daemon=bug vs incapable) and revises agent_supports instead. The daemon-side marker evidence they asked for is answered in full above and remains true regardless of the agent-level finding; it is kept in this cell's record because a future scenario or re-assessment may need it.

The agent_supports=no call rests on treating a delayed-birth startup gate as not satisfying this row's ready->working->waiting requirement -- a standard this assessment did not invent, but adopted directly from the already-committed codex and antigravity sibling cells' own explicit reasoning for their structurally identical trust/hook prompts. If a future maintainer decides that standard is too strict and a startup gate should count for this row after all, muse's verdict should flip back to agent_supports=yes with the daemon-pillar findings above already reasoned out for that case (daemon=bug, buildable via sessionIDFromPath recognizing the marker).

VACUOUS-PASS CONDITION (kept for the daemon findings' benefit even though this cell is frozen at the agent level): any future spec exercising the marker must independently prove the modal was on screen (a pane capture) before crediting any state derived from marker presence, exactly as the claudecode/codex/antigravity siblings require for their own class-2 dialogs.

LOAD-BEARING ENVIRONMENT PROPERTY for every probe in this cell: $RUN_CWD must be a directory muse has never seen before -- a previously-trusted directory (per settings persisted somewhere under muse's data dir; not located precisely in this pass) skips the dialog entirely, confirmed live by relaunching in an already-trusted cwd.

Both live-kill probes and the relaunch-in-trusted-cwd probe ran in this shared, concurrently-used environment (other onboarding subagents had muse sessions live at the same time); the exact UUIDs and timestamps quoted are specific to this run but the STRUCTURE (marker exists, is durable, matches the final id, gets consumed on trust, orphans on kill, does not recur once trusted) was independently reproduced across three separate launches and is the load-bearing part.

This assessment probed live rather than relying only on static reads, consistent with the shared context's guidance that a plausible-looking negative on this column has been wrong before. Here the deeper live probe changed the conclusion twice in the same session (first toward incapable, then toward a no-agent-support finding after the coordinator's review) -- both corrections came from checking rather than assuming, which is the point of the rule.

sources.note: The established standard this cell now follows: codex's own trust prompts (cwd_prompt.rs, startup_hooks_review.rs) are explicitly excluded from this row as delayed-birth startup gates with 'no working->waiting edge'; agent_supports=yes there rests solely on a mid-session MCP elicitation trigger.
"The other three triggers the row lists do not qualify on codex" -- the meta-only frozen-cell convention this cell's expected.jsonl follows.

agy's own trust gate: 'blocks BEFORE agy mints the conversation dir/transcript, so no session exists yet' -- the same structural finding as muse's, but agy keeps agent_supports=yes via its independently-existing MCP elicitation support, which muse lacks.

sessionIDFromPath: `if filepath.Base(path) != transcriptFilename { return "" }`, transcriptFilename = "session.jsonl" (exact match). Both .session.lock and .session.jsonl.permission-init fail this check today; this is the specific line the coordinator's review asked about.
Source() returns agent.FilesUnderRoot{Dir: defaultRootDir, SessionIDFromPath: sessionIDFromPath, ...} -- the only transport into muse session data; no hook mechanism is declared.

DiscoverPID(cwd, transcriptPath string, ...) takes an already-known transcriptPath -- relevant to the orphan-marker question: PID/process-liveness reconciliation already exists in this adapter's design, independent of which file resolves the session id.

sources.ref: tmux sessions musetp3/musetp3b/musetp4, this assessment (coordinator-review pass), 2026-09-14
sources.note: Three fresh-cwd launches. musetp3: session dir 01a09f2f-0e1e-7020-8cfd-ba4b87d6a206 inspected via lsof-located path while the dialog was up (t=0 and t=20s+, unchanged sha256), then dismissed (Enter) -- .session.jsonl.permission-init disappeared, session.jsonl appeared in the same dir with an identical first line. musetp3b: muse relaunched in the SAME now-trusted cwd -- no dialog, straight to composer. musetp4: session dir 01a09f30-a704-79a3-85b5-fc644431349c, process SIGKILL'd while the dialog was still undecided -- directory left permanently orphaned with only the two pre-session files.

sources.ref: muse-bin-strings.txt (11.9MB strings dump of /Users/ingo/.local/bin/muse, captured this task's earlier pass and re-checked here)
sources.note: 'elicitation', 'auto-mode', 'managed_settings', 'settings review', 'needs your input' all ABSENT; the only session-marker filename variant anywhere in the binary or on disk (scanned every muse session directory on this host) is 'permission-init' -- a single, deliberate, versioned mechanism ('reminder-child-permission-init-transaction-v1'), not an incidental temp file.
--trust-workspace / --yolo are the only workspace-trust controls; sandbox is a standalone subcommand; mcp only handles OAuth login/logout; no auto-mode/settings-review command or flag.

recipe.notes: applicable: false. muse has no dialog matching this row's required ready->working->waiting shape: its one tool-free blocking dialog (workspace trust) fires before any session/ready state exists (live-verified: the trust prompt is the literal first thing the pane shows, no banner or composer precedes it), and it has no sandbox/network confirmation, MCP elicitation, or auto-mode/settings-review dialog at all (binary-strings-confirmed absent). RE-ASSESS WHEN muse ships a mid-session, tool-free blocking dialog (most plausibly MCP elicitation, since muse already has an `mcp` OAuth subcommand as a foundation) -- at that point the daemon-side finding already reasoned out in this cell's body applies directly: recognizing .session.jsonl.permission-init's directory-derived session id in sessionIDFromPath (or a sibling function) is a buildable, non-guessing extension, confirmed via three live probes to carry the session's real final id with no collision risk on the happy path, modulo an orphan case on an abandoned/killed launch that the existing process-liveness reconciliation already covers.
